question: Your team uses Claude Code in CI to review pull requests for a payments service. Each finding gets one of three severity levels: blocker, warning, or note, and any blocker stops the merge. Developers complain that a missing input check in the same API handler was a blocker on Monday and a note on Thursday. The review prompt currently says only that Claude should assign a severity that reflects the risk of the issue. Which change to the prompt would most effectively make these severity assignments consistent?

options.text: Ask Claude to report a confidence score from 1 to 10 with each finding, and downgrade any blocker whose score falls below seven.
options.reason: The guide says review criteria should be specific rather than relying on confidence-based filtering, so a score threshold does not define what each level means.

options.text: Tell Claude to be careful and conservative, and to assign the blocker level only when it is highly confident about the risk of the finding.
options.reason: The guide says general instructions such as being conservative or reporting only high-confidence findings fail to improve precision compared to specific categorical criteria.

options.text: Rewrite the severity instruction as a longer paragraph that stresses why consistent severity matters to developers, while still leaving the three levels undefined.
options.reason: The guide says explicit criteria work better than vague instructions, and a longer emphasis on consistency still gives no criteria or examples for each level.

options.text: Define explicit criteria for blocker, warning, and note, and give a concrete code example of a typical finding for each of the three levels.
options.reason: The guide says explicit severity criteria with concrete code examples for each severity level achieve consistent classification.
